title: A booking moved, and a price doubt the junior operator steps over
demonstrates: Slot 6's weak spot in writing, as in her calls: a time first and a clean summary, and when the customer says another shop is cheaper she soothes ('I totally understand') and does not answer. The draft she wrote over had the answer. The booking holds anyway; she sends the closing draft as it was, labels, resolves.

customer.name: Reggie Dorsey
customer.note: a customer of the East Main shop with an alignment booked for the Monday

scenario.who_writes: A customer with an appointment he cannot keep.
scenario.what_happens: He asks to move Monday's alignment. The assistant cannot see appointments and hands over. Maya moves it and offers two times; he takes Thursday at 8:00 and asks whether the price is really 120 when another shop charges 89. She reassures him and confirms the time.

facts: the booking was moved by slot 6 four minutes after the hand-off
the customer voiced a price doubt (120 against 89 elsewhere) and it was not answered: she reassured and confirmed the time

why: 'I totally understand' is where an answer should be; her call scores show the same thing (story S4, objection).
The discarded draft is the better reply, and the outcome row is the evidence.
Everything else is her at her best: four minutes, two times, the address in the last line.
